aisha_named: true: as 'Axa' in the 1652 English ('the said Axa, who was Ubequar's Daughter'); the Spanish original spelling was NOT read
age_mentioned: true: six years old at marriage; 'eight years old' at consummation ('when she was but eight years old')
famous: true: cited by en.wikipedia 'Aisha' article (note 48, the 1652 book, pp. 229-30) and 'Juan Andrés (convert)' article; no scholarly treatment of this passage read
ref: Juan Andrés, The Confusion of Muhamed's Sect (London, 1652; trans. 'I. N.'), closing paragraph after the heading CHAP. XII (EEBO-TCP text line 296). The author says he 'forgot to set down in the Chapter of wives' (Chap. VII, text line 195). Page: Wikipedia cites pp. 229-30; NOT checked against a page image.
quote_en: You must know that Muhamed contracted marriage with the said Axa, who was Ubequar's Daughter, when she was six years old; and consummated the said Marriage with her, when she was but eight years old; which thing I prove by the said book Azar, upon which I would ask thee, O Moor, and would have thee resolve me, whether it was fit for Muhamed to consummate Marriage with a little girl of eight years old? which is almost a homicide, and a sin against nature, especially in such a man as Muhamed, and who at that time had seven wives together. Speak, O Moor, in God's Name, was it not a great vice? and was he not a man Luxurious beyond measure?
licence_note: 1652 English: pre-1931, public domain. Read from the EEBO-TCP transcription on distantreader (plain text, not page image; transcription errors possible). The Spanish 1515 text and the Latin 1595 / German 1685 texts were NOT read, so quote_orig is empty.
keys: a little girl of eight years old
keys_note: English substrings of quote_en, because quote_orig is unavailable.
what_it_says: Andrés says Muhammad married Aisha ('Axa') when she was six and consummated the marriage when she was eight, which he calls almost a homicide and a sin against nature, and notes Muhammad then had seven wives.
context: The closing paragraph of a polemic by a former Muslim who became a Catholic priest; it is part of his attack on Muhammad's character and marriages, and he cites a book he calls 'Azar' as his source. The surrounding text is anti-Islamic polemic throughout and quotes Qur'anic and Sunni material he claims to have read.
limits: (1) English translation only; the Spanish wording and original spelling were not read. (2) Ages are six and eight, not the Islamic six and nine: report the discrepancy. (3) The source 'book Azar' is unidentified. (4) The author is an ex-Muslim polemicist: his statements are his own, but polemical and unverified against Arabic sources. (5) The claim 'one of the earliest explicit condemnations' (Wikipedia) rests only on this book; the scholarly source it cites (Szpiech 2012, p. 318) was not accessed. (6) Transcription from EEBO-TCP; spelling is 1652 English. (7) Wikipedia calls him 'Spanish Catholic'; he was a convert from Islam (fl. 1487-1515 per Wikipedia).
